claim_tested: Type I error of stopping rules on a crossed design (lme4 1.1-35.1, REML, Satterthwaite via lmerTest 3.1-3)
design: 24 subjects x 16 items, one +-0.5 factor within subject and item (Latin square); intercept SDs .5; slope SD tau for subjects and items; rho .3; sigma 1
result: Rejection at .05 for tau = 0 / .1 / .2 / .4: maximal .025/.016/.037/.037; protected back-off (focal slopes never dropped) .032/.018/.040/.037; back-off on singular-or-nonconvergent .043/.031/.055/.050; LRT(.2) data order .044/.033/.057/.043; LRT(.2) design order .045/.033/.055/.045; AIC .047/.036/.059/.055; LRT(.05) .055/.042/.068/.080; intercepts only .059/.043/.084/.200
files: sim/sim1_stopping_rules.R; sim/out/rerun/sim1_S24_I16_*.csv (rerun with protected strategy; shared strategies reproduced exactly: 8,000/8,000 p-values identical); sim/out/sim1_summary_small.csv

claim_tested: Singular and non-convergence rates of the maximal model
result: Maximal fit singular (isSingular, tol 1e-4) in 83% / 79% / 67% / 27% of data sets for tau = 0/.1/.2/.4; convergence warnings 2.5% / 2.3% / 1.9% / 1.1%

claim_tested: Does data-driven removal of the lower-level slope inflate Type I error for a cross-level interaction (Heisig & Schaeffer 2019)?
design: J clusters x 20 pupils; x within-cluster centred; z cluster-level; slope SD tau1; intercept SD .5; test of x:z

claim_tested: Is dropping a nuisance slope before the focal slope safe for the focal test?
design: 30 units x 20 obs; focal x1 and nuisance x2 within units, correlation r; both slope SDs .3; zero-correlation fits
result: H0, r = 0: full .059, drop nuisance slope .054, drop focal slope .226, intercept only .226. H0, r = .5: .039 / .035 / .187 / .173. Power (beta1 = .15), r = .5: full .482, drop nuisance .447 (mean SE .0741 vs .0795); r = 0: .550 vs .560

claim_tested: Are zero-correlation models invariant to coding?
design: 30 subjects x 20 obs, 2-level factor coded 0/1 vs -0.5/+0.5; 3-level factor with '||'
result: Unstructured: identical REML criterion (1773.273) and slope SE (0.10072) under both codings. Zero-correlation: REML 1773.664 vs 1774.988, SE 0.10306 vs 0.10072, Satterthwaite df 31.3 vs 29.0. lme4 1.1-35.1: (1 + f3 || s) kept 7 covariance parameters including correlations among indicator columns; numeric sum-contrast columns gave 3

claim_tested: Is a likelihood-based random-effects ladder invariant to the focal fixed effect (basis for masked execution)?
design: 200 crossed data sets x 4 rungs, y vs y + 3.7*A, REML and ML
result: REML: max abs change in theta 0.00103, in REML criterion 1.7e-4; singular flag and warning status identical in 799/800 fits each; estimate shifted by exactly 3.7 (error 3e-14). ML: max change in deviance 3.0e-5; singular flag identical in 798/800

claim_tested: Do the Sim1 patterns hold with more subjects and items?
design: 48 subjects x 32 items; otherwise as Sim1-small; beta = .18 for H1
reps: 500 per cell (MCSE about .01 at .05; .02 for power)
result: H0 at tau = .2 / .4: maximal .044/.056; protected back-off .044/.056; back-off singular-or-nonconvergent .052/.058; LRT(.2) .052/.056; AIC .060/.056; LRT(.05) .080/.056; intercepts only .146/.348. Power at tau = .2 / .4: maximal .712/.392; protected .710/.392; back-off .724/.392; LRT(.2) .724-.728/.392; AIC .738/.392. Maximal fit singular in 29% (tau .2) and 0.4% (tau .4); convergence warnings 4.0% and 1.0%

claim_tested: Is keeping a zero-variance focal slope (singular protected rung) inference-neutral relative to dropping it? Where does the back-off rule's extra power come from?
design: Sim1-small design, tau 0 and .1, beta .25; zero-correlation rung fitted; when singular, refit without exactly the slope terms estimated at zero
result: SE ratio keep/drop: median |ratio - 1| = 3e-6, max 0.026; Satterthwaite df median 22.2 vs 22.2; rejection .59 vs .59. Keeping a zero-variance term is inference-neutral, so the power gain of the fixed-ladder back-off in Sim1 comes from its next rung also removing a non-zero slope when a different term is singular (removal of small non-zero variances, as LRT(.2) does)
